155.body:
The mocked E2E job on #147 (JiuwenSwarm backend) was red, and it could not say why: the job summary and the uploaded artifact were empty. Working through it turned up one sandbox escape, one hang in the adapter, two product gaps in which tools JiuwenSwarm offers, and a set of stale or mis-configured tests. This PR fixes each at its cause. The results-path fix and the host-tools fix landed with #147; what is here is the rest.

## Nested `task` runs no longer hang the parent (Known gap 10)

**Root cause.** Every run's tools go to JiuwenSwarm through one shared MCP server, `sci`. When a run brought a tool or argument the shared list did not have, `ensure_shared_tools` gave JiuwenSwarm the new list by `mcp.disconnect` / `delete_custom` / `register_custom` / `connect` of that same server — and `mcp.disconnect` is global. A `task` sub-agent's run starts while its parent is waiting on that very `task` call, brings tools the list did not have, and so cut the parent's call in flight: the parent never got its result and hung until its timeout. JiuwenSwarm's own log of a stuck `journey-session-trajectory` run shows it to the second: the parent's `task` call at 06:19:27, the disconnect of `sci` at 06:19:28, the sub-agent's session at 06:19:29, then nothing. That is why the failure looked "load-sensitive": it depends on whether the child happens to bring something new to the shared list at that moment.

**Fix.** A changed list goes to the next generation's server name (`sci` + ten digits). Runs already on the old name keep it; it is disconnected only when the last of them ends. Approval levels are re-applied under the new name, and the proxy's history-prefix regex covers every generation. New adapter test: `test_new_tools_never_disconnect_the_server_a_running_run_is_calling_through`.

## JiuwenSwarm's planning and delegation tools are hidden when they are not the run's

With JiuwenSwarm's tools on (the default), all of its tools are offered — including `todo_*` when the project's Plan plugin is switched off, and `subagent_*` when delegation is ScienceDiscovery's `task`. The model could then plan or delegate around the project's composition and the run's settings. They now go into `hiddenJiuwenSwarmTools` in those cases, and JiuwenSwarm plans only in place of an `update_plan` the run actually has (as delegation already required `task`). Found by `journey-plugin-composition` once the journeys ran on JiuwenSwarm's tools.

## The journeys run on JiuwenSwarm's own tools

`run-e2e.sh` pinned `SCIENCE_AGENT_JIUWENSWARM_TOOLS=ours` and `PLANNING=update_plan` for the journeys, while the JiuwenSwarm live checks that run afterwards against the same stack test the shipped defaults — so `skills` and `skill-switch` could only fail (they were masked until now by the host-tools failure ahead of them). The layer now runs the product's defaults, with one exception: `SUBAGENTS=task`, because a `subagent_spawn` sub-agent has none of the tools, sandbox, deliverables or sub-agent cards the delegation journeys are about (Known gap 1a). Journeys moved accordingly: `journey-plan-workspace` plans with `todo_create`/`todo_modify`, `journey-compact-process` loads skill-creator with `skill_tool`, `journey-plugin-composition` checks `todo_create` as the Plan tool.

## Tests that were wrong

- **`live.mjs approvals`** still required a `jiuwenswarm`-sourced authorization row. 53933a8 deliberately stopped double-booking an asked call, so there is exactly one record per call — the user's answer. The check now asserts that: two records, allowed and denied, one per tool call.
- **J11 `journey-skill-folder-import`** timed out before the product saw a file: Playwright/Chromium's directory upload never returns for a path with non-ASCII characters, and `testInfo.outputPath()` carries this test's Chinese title (reproduced standalone: ASCII path 47 ms, CJK path hangs). The folders now go to an ASCII `mkdtemp` directory.
- **`literature-review` "Connector 未启用时的失败反馈"** was a permanent `test.fixme` because the paper-search form it drove was removed. Rewritten around the MCP flow: with arXiv off in the Composer's connector picker, a scripted model's `mcp__arxiv__search` call fails visibly in the conversation, the model was never offered an arXiv tool, no arXiv invocation is recorded and the Run still completes; enabling arXiv gives the next Run `mcp__arxiv__search`. arXiv is never reached. It is back in the shared plan (`@mocked`, `@model:mock`; its `status:unreviewed` row leaves `test/support/tagged/MIGRATION.md`).

Docs: `jiuwenswarm-migration-status.md` (en, zh) — row 95 and Known gap 10.

## Validation

Validation for this head is the GitHub Actions run on this pull request (UT, ST, E2E mocked, both binary builds, Docker image); the layers were not re-run locally on the merge commit. Before the merge with the current `feat/jiuwenswarm`, on this branch:

- Adapter pytest: 171 passed, 8 skipped.
- `jiuwenswarm-agent` API tests: 64/64.
- Mocked E2E on the JiuwenSwarm backend (the old `run-e2e.sh` layer): 41 passed / 1 failed / 2 skipped, and all 9 JiuwenSwarm live checks ok (`history`, `history-names`, `run-shell`, `host-tools`, `approvals`, `skills`, `skill-switch`, `trajectory`, `language`). The one failure, `journey-plugin-composition`, is fixed by the last API commit and passed on re-run together with `journey-plan-workspace`. The two skips were J3 (`SCIENTIFIC_ENVS=0` in the mocked layer, by design) and the literature-review fixme rewritten here.

The merge brought in #154's tagged shared plan, which now selects and gates these journeys; this PR's first CI run is the first time they run under it.

## E2E user journeys

Tested on the JiuwenSwarm backend, browser journeys against an isolated local stack, before the merge:

| Journey | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `journey-session-trajectory` (main + `task` sub-agent) | FAIL — run stuck `running` for 180 s | PASS |
| `journey-compact-process` | FAIL — only after earlier journeys | PASS |
| `journey-skill-folder-import` (J11) | FAIL — 120 s timeout | PASS (5.1 s) |
| `journey-plan-workspace` on todo tools | — | PASS |
| `journey-plugin-composition` on JiuwenSwarm tools | FAIL — `todo_create` offered with Plan off | PASS |
| `literature-review` connector failure | fixme (never ran) | PASS (jiuwenswarm 35.4 s, legacy 5.8 s) |
| J3 `journey-prepare-environment` | BLOCKED | BLOCKED — scientific environments are off in the mocked layer |

Known and not fixed here: in one of four default-mode runs of `live.mjs approvals`, JiuwenSwarm accepted the approval answer and then never made the tool call; logs recorded, cause not yet found. The 17 `server.test.ts` sub-agent cases kept out as `status:unreviewed` for gap 10 can be revisited separately now that the stall's cause is fixed.

## Release

Release category: release:fix (label pending a maintainer)
User impact: a run that delegates with `task` no longer hangs when its sub-agent brings new tools; switching off the Plan plugin, or keeping delegation on `task`, now really withdraws JiuwenSwarm's own planning or delegation tools.
Compatibility and migration: none. The adapter registers extra MCP server names (`sci0000000001`, …) with JiuwenSwarm as tool lists change and removes each once idle.

156.author: Birfy
156.body:
## Context

I branched `test/jiuwenswarm-e2e` from `feat/jiuwenswarm` (46676a0) and deployed it with `./scripts/start-stack.sh --mode local --jiuwenswarm`. Then I used the main features in a real browser (Playwright + Chromium) with a real model: Kimi `kimi-for-coding` at `https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1`. That testing found the five problems below. After each fix I checked it again in the browser.

## Fixes

### 1. `run_shell` fails when the model passes the workspace's absolute host path as `cwd` (a433c613)
JiuwenSwarm gives the model the host path of its working directory (in `trusted_dirs`). The model then passes that path unchanged as `cwd`. The Runner refuses it with `cwd must be workspace-relative`. The model retries the same call, which shows another approval card.
Fix: a new `workspaceRelativeCwd` in `packages/workspace` makes a cwd that names the workspace relative. That covers the host path and the sandbox's `/workspace`. Any other absolute path is left unchanged, so the Runner still refuses it.

### 2. A call denied at JiuwenSwarm's approval question leaves no trace in the timeline (33b59367)
Only the bridge reports our tools, and it does so when it runs them. A denied call never reaches the bridge. So the approval card disappeared and nothing replaced it. The call's announcement also stayed pending, so a later call with the same arguments could claim it.
Fix: the adapter reports the call as completed. If the bridge never claimed it, `EventTranslator` withdraws the announcement and reports the call itself: a start, then a failed end. It also adds the result to the model-facing transcript. A call the bridge ran is still reported once.

### 3. `$` in messages rendered as LaTeX (902364e0)
`remark-math` treats any two single dollars as inline math. So a command like `for i in $(seq 1 120); do echo tick $i; done`, or prices like `$5 and $10`, rendered as garbled KaTeX. This affects both backends.
Fix: before rendering, every single `$` that Pandoc would not read as a math delimiter is escaped. Pandoc's rule is:
- the opening `$` is followed by a non-space character;
- the closing `$` is preceded by a non-space character and not followed by a digit;
- the formula stays within one paragraph.

`$$…$$`, `\$` that is already escaped, fenced code and inline code are left as they are.

### 4. Session naming fails for models that accept only their own temperature (c796268a)
Session naming sends `temperature: 0`. Kimi's coding models answer 400 (`invalid temperature: only 1 is allowed for this model`). The existing fallback only dropped the `thinking` flag. So every session kept its truncated first message as its title, and the log kept showing `Session naming model failed with HTTP 400`.
Fix: a 400/422 gets one more try without `temperature`, so the provider uses its own default.

### 5. The sign-in link of a `--jiuwenswarm` stack names the internal port (2f30b21b)
The adapter takes the public port 4310 and the API moves to 4410. The API still printed an "Open to sign in" link on 4410, which bypasses the adapter.
Fix: `start-stack.sh` passes the public port to the API as `SCIENCE_AGENT_PUBLIC_PORT`, and the sign-in link uses it. When the variable is not set, the link is unchanged.

## Verification

**Live browser testing (Kimi, JiuwenSwarm backend):**
- Created a project and session from the UI and sent tasks.
- Approvals: a card left open for 5–8 s, then approved, runs the command. A denied call now shows as "call failed: run_shell".
- Multi-turn: the second turn reads the file the first turn wrote.
- Stop: the run stops within 1 s and the composer can start a new run.
- CSV upload → regression → a PNG figure and a summary CSV as artifacts. The figure preview and its provenance work (derived from `growth.csv v1` → `run_shell` → full script).
- All 17 system configuration pages open. The "Connect model" wizard connected Kimi as a custom provider and registered 4 models.
- Trajectory view shows the timeline, the exact model inputs and outputs, reasoning, and tool calls.
- UI language: after switching to English, JiuwenSwarm answers in English even to a Chinese question.
- Subagent delegation with web search (`subagent_spawn` / `wait` / `close`): the conclusion comes with source links.

**Automated tests:**
- `services/adapter`: pytest passes.
- `services/api`: `jiuwenswarm-agent` 66/66, `session-naming` 12/12, `bootstrap-tokens` 14/14, including new tests for the fixes above.
- `packages/workspace`: 76/76.
- `apps/web`: 844/844, and typecheck passes.
- Mocked browser E2E suite (`.ci/run-e2e.sh mocked`, JiuwenSwarm backend): TBD.

## Known issues (not addressed here)

- After Stop, a managed `run_shell` execution keeps running in the sandbox. `docs/en/core/execution-workspaces.md` says this is by design ("only explicit cancellation stops the job"). `docs/en/reference/runtime-behavior.md` says Stop kills in-flight Bubblewrap execution. The two docs need to agree.
- A provider migrated from standalone model profiles has no API key by design. Still, the model registry asks it for its model list every time it opens, gets a 502, and logs a browser console error.
- The approval card shows the same command text in both its title and its body.

156.title: JiuwenSwarm backend fixes from live testing: absolute cwd, denied calls in the timeline, $ rendered as math, session naming, sign-in port

Since #154, the E2E job's log shows the preparation steps, `Frozen 43 identities`, and then nothing until the plan's summary line. No journey passes or fails in it, and no Playwright error appears; reading why a journey failed means downloading the whole `e2e-results` artifact, about 90 MB. Before #154 the job ran `.ci/run-e2e.sh` directly and its output was the job log.

## Echo the E2E driver's output

The shared runner starts `.ci/run-e2e.sh` through `run()` in `test/support/tagged/shared.mjs`, which collected the child's stdout and stderr in memory and wrote them to `e2e-driver.log` when it exited. `run()` now takes `{ echo: true }`, which also passes the output through as it arrives, and only the E2E driver sets it. `run-e2e.sh` tees everything it prints into `run.log` itself, so the job log reads as it did before #154: the stack coming up, each journey as it passes or fails, Playwright's error blocks, and the JiuwenSwarm checks. `e2e-driver.log` and the artifact are unchanged.

The other `run()` callers (preparation, command checks, coverage merging) stay quiet; each of them names its log when it fails.

`main` has the same code: `test/support/tagged/shared.mjs` came from it with #154. The same commit goes to `main` in its own pull request.

## Validation

GitHub Actions on `9ef1b960`, this commit on `feat/jiuwenswarm` at `fa11c46f` (run 35841836435), every job green: UT 3463 planned, executed and passed; ST; E2E 44/44/44; Coverage, the Docker image and both binary releases. The E2E job's log carries every journey on its own line, 44 of them, Playwright's `44 passed (13.7m)`, and the nine JiuwenSwarm checks, each `ok`.

For comparison, CI dispatched on `feat/jiuwenswarm` itself at the same `fa11c46f` (run 35841746993), without this commit: E2E 44/44/44 as well, and its log has no journey line and no check line. The outcome is the same; only what the log shows differs.

On the base before #153 (`2d547ce5`), this commit's E2E failed `journey-prepare-environment` J3 twice: `expandToolStep` clicked the run_shell card and it stayed closed. On `fa11c46f` J3 passes both with and without this commit.

The same commit on `main` (#158) ran E2E locally and in its own CI at 43 of 43, each journey on the console.

## E2E user journeys

Not applicable as a product change: this changes what the E2E layer prints, not what it runs or selects. The evidence is this pull request's own E2E job log.

## Release

Release category: release:internal

User impact: none in the product. The E2E job log shows the journeys again.

158.author: zhaozhaozz
158.body:
Three defects in the tagged test harness and its workflow, found while bringing it to `feat/jiuwenswarm` in #154, where each did visible harm. They are on `main` too; here they have been harmless or only inconvenient so far, and would not stay that way. On `feat/jiuwenswarm` the first two came with #154 and the third is #157.

## pytest reads each Python project's own config

`test/support/tagged/coordinator.mjs` passed the science_tags plugin's options as two arguments, `--science-root <repo>`. pytest locates its config file before a `-p` plugin has declared its options, so at that point `<repo>` is a positional argument, a test path, and the search starts from the repository root. `services/<name>/pyproject.toml` was never read. On `main` nothing depended on it yet (`evolve` and `memory-graph` set only `testpaths`, which explicit file arguments override); on `feat/jiuwenswarm` it made all 85 of the adapter's `async def` tests fail, because its `asyncio_mode = "auto"` never applied. Each option now goes as one token, `--science-root=<repo>`.

The new integration test lays a project out as `services/<name>/` is, a config one level below the root the harness is given, with `asyncio_mode = "auto"` in it and a conftest that declares the option as pytest-asyncio does. It fails on the old coordinator (`assert 'strict' == 'auto'`) and passes on the new one.

## The layers' results are uploaded

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` uploads `.ci-results` as `ut-results`, `st-results` and `e2e-results`. upload-artifact@v4 leaves out anything whose name starts with a dot, the given path included, so all three uploaded nothing: each step only warned "No files were found with the provided path: .ci-results" and stayed green (run 35801037405 on #150 shows it for all three). The steps now set `include-hidden-files: true`, as the two coverage uploads already did. The only dot-file inside is Playwright's `.last-run.json`.

A test in `.ci/ci-contract.test.mjs` reads every workflow and requires `include-hidden-files: true` on any upload whose path goes through a dot-directory. Against the old `ci.yml` it names exactly the three results steps.

## The E2E job log shows the journeys

The shared runner starts `.ci/run-e2e.sh` through `run()` in `test/support/tagged/shared.mjs`, which collected the child's output in memory and wrote it to `e2e-driver.log` when it exited. So the E2E job printed the preparation, `Frozen 43 identities`, and then nothing until the summary: no journey passing or failing and no Playwright error. Run 35829671368 on `main` has 446 log lines and not one from Playwright; reading why a journey failed meant downloading the artifact, which the previous section shows was empty. `run()` now takes `{ echo: true }`, which also passes the output through as it arrives, and only the E2E driver sets it. `run-e2e.sh` tees everything it prints into `run.log`, so the job log reads as it did before the plan: the stack coming up, each journey, Playwright's error blocks. `e2e-driver.log` is unchanged, and the other `run()` callers (preparation, command checks, coverage merging) stay quiet, each naming its log when it fails.

## Validation

Local, profile `pr`.

| Layer | planned | executed | passed | failed | skipped |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pnpm ci:ut -- --coverage` | 3162 | 3162 | 3143 | 19 | 0 |
| `pnpm ci:st -- --coverage` | 1 | 1 | 1 | 0 | 0 |
| `pnpm ci:e2e` | 43 | 43 | 43 | 0 | 0 |

UT's 19 failures are `services/runner`'s `egress-gateway.test.ts` (16), `sandbox-network.test.ts` (2) and `server.test.ts` (1), and they are the host, not the change: that run had `TMPDIR` in a deep checkout path, and each failure reads "the egress socket path is N bytes, over this platform's 107-byte Unix socket path limit". The same three files with a short `TMPDIR` pass 77 of 77. None of them touches the harness or the workflow. UT and ST ran on the first two commits before a rebase onto `94de21ce`, a documentation change; the third commit changes only what the E2E slice prints.

Every Python project passes through the coordinator now that its config is read: paper, gateway, memory-graph and evolve are all in the UT run above with no failure.

The E2E run's console, which carried nothing from Playwright before this change, now has every journey on its own line, 43 of them, and Playwright's `43 passed (8.4m)`; `e2e-driver.log` still has the same output.

Both new tests are planned identities and passed in that UT run: the contract test directly, and the integration test inside `check:tagged-selftest` (47 of 47). `pnpm ci:selftest` 11/11.

GitHub Actions on `a5602d3d` (run 35835373565), every job green: UT 3162 planned, executed and passed; ST 1/1/1; E2E 43/43/43; Coverage, the Docker image and both binary releases. The runner files that failed locally pass there. `ut-results` now uploads 1928 files and `e2e-results` 534, where each had 0. The E2E job's log carries every journey on its own line, 43 of them, and Playwright's `43 passed (8.5m)`.

## E2E user journeys

PASS. Tested on the tree of `a5602d3d`; `pnpm ci:e2e`, the mocked browser subset on an isolated local stack. 43 planned, 43 executed, 43 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped. This change adds no user-observable product path; the third fix changes what the layer prints, and this run is also its evidence.

## Release

Release category: release:internal

User impact: none in the product. A project's pytest config applies in the gate, CI keeps its UT, ST and E2E results, and the E2E job log shows the journeys.

Compatibility and migration: none.

162.author: zhaozhaozz
162.body:
The Node.js and Python coverage summaries (`node-coverage-summary-*`, `python-coverage-summary-*`) carry whole-repository totals, per-group totals and a file count per group, but not the files themselves. A reader of those artifacts can therefore show coverage by directory group and never by file; the project status board wants a directory tree that expands down to individual files. This change adds each measured file's own totals to both summaries.

## Node.js summary: `sources`

`scripts/coverage-summary.mjs` exports `sourceTotals(records)` and writes `sources` into the summary: one entry per measured source with its repository-relative `path` and its `lines`, `branches` and `functions` totals, sorted by path. The entries come from the same records the group and overall totals are built from, so they add up to those totals exactly; nothing is measured twice or re-parsed.

## Python summary: `sources`

`scripts/python-coverage-summary.mjs` does the same for Python in `summarizePythonCoverage`, keeps the list in `pythonSummaryDocument`, and merges the lists of all groups in `aggregatePythonCoverage` (sorted by path) so the aggregated document lists every file once.

The field is additive: existing fields keep their names and values, and readers that ignore unknown keys are unaffected. The compressed artifacts grow modestly (in a test-repository run, the Node.js summary artifact went from about 40 KB to 75 KB and the Python one from about 7 KB to 11 KB).

## Validation

Local layers on `3bda6a1f` (this branch's head), `CI_RESULTS_DIR=.tmp/ci-results CI_RUNTIME_DIR=.tmp/ci-runtime`:

- `pnpm ci:ut`: 3162 planned / 3162 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped across 315 test files, including the updated `scripts/coverage-summary.test.mjs` and `scripts/python-coverage-summary.test.mjs`.
- `pnpm ci:st`: smoke 1 planned / 1 passed (`test/api/agent_loop_smoke.ts`).
- `pnpm ci:e2e` (mocked browser subset): 43 planned / 43 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped with a fresh runtime directory. Two earlier attempts that reused one runtime directory each blocked one journey (J3 in `journey-prepare-environment`, then one in `journey-compact-process`) at the managed Python base, whose `micromamba create --channel conda-forge` download failed after retries on this host. That step does not touch the coverage scripts; unmodified `main` (`60bc099e`) in a separate detached worktree passed 43/43, and so did the GitHub-hosted E2E job on this commit (below).

The same commit also ran the full `.github/workflows/ci.yml` on a pull request in a test repository that shares this repository's history; every job passed: UT 3162/3162, ST 1/1, E2E (mocked) 43 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped, both Binary release jobs, Docker image and Coverage. A later `workflow_dispatch` run of that repository's `main` with this change merged published summaries whose `sources` list 486 Node.js and 69 Python files; summed over those files, the totals equal the summaries' own totals exactly (Node.js lines 94158 / 129215 and branches 35036 / 54867; Python lines 5852 / 9241 and branches 1509 / 3236).

## E2E user journeys

PASS for the mocked browser subset on the tested SHA (numbers above). This change has no product UI, API or CLI path of its own: it only adds a field to the JSON the CI coverage step uploads. Its consumer journey is reading the uploaded summary: the test-repository run above uploaded `node-coverage-summary-*` and `python-coverage-summary-*` with `sources`, and a dashboard reading them rendered the per-file directory tree from them.

## Release

Release category: release:internal
User impact: none for product users; the CI coverage summary artifacts now list each measured file with its own totals.
Compatibility and migration: none; `sources` is a new field and all existing fields are unchanged.
